STEP 1:
THE TIME BASED RANGES

But every single one of them sits inside something called a dealing range.
So before I give you the times, I have to show you how I find those.
A dealing range is just the space between a significant swing high and a swing low…
And a swing high or low simply means a point where the market turned around.
LIVE
So this was the low that pushed the market higher, and this was the high that pushed the market lower.
Draw a line at each, and automatically that becomes a range to the market.
That's it, super easy.
Now why does that actually matter? Because of what sits above and below those 2 lines.
LIVE
An order is just you telling the market "if price gets here, I'm in"...
You set it…
You walk away, and it fires by itself when price arrives.
And everyone looking at this chart can see that high and that low, same as you can, so they all leave their orders in roughly the same place.
Which means there's a stack of them sat right there, waiting to get filled.
That's all liquidity means…
Orders waiting to get filled.
And the market doesn't move to random places, it moves to where those orders are.
Now, those 2 lines still don't tell you when any of it happens, because that box could be days wide.
And that's exactly where my time based ranges come in.

STEP 2:
THE BIAS
So we've got our 2 boxes, and they tell us where the orders are and when the market's going to go for them.
What they don't tell us yet is which way we're trading.
And this is the part everyone assumes is the hard part, because everybody will tell you that you can't predict the market.
That's not true...
Predicting is exactly what we're doing here… it's the whole point.
The difference is WHAT you're predicting from.
Most traders just predict from an opinion…
They check the news, glance at a higher timeframe, decide the market feels bearish, and hope they're right.
That's not a prediction.
That's a guess with a nicer word on it.
And here's what that actually looked like on a normal day a couple of years ago:
Market spikes
You buy
It reverses
Stops you out
You're annoyed, so you flip and sell
And it reverses again
Anyone done that?

With nothing in front of you to base it on.
Long or short… Biggest decision of your day, and you're making it under that kind of pressure.
Nobody gets that right consistently.
So we don't pick a direction at all…
We let the market pick it for us.
Because before the market can go anywhere, it has to go and collect the orders sitting on one side first.
And you already know exactly where those orders are, because you marked them in step 1.
So the market walks into one of your boxes, and the second it does, it's told you which way you're going.

2- Then the dealing range extreme has to go too

Remember what we said is sitting below that low?
A stack of sell orders, from people selling the breakdown and people getting stopped out.
Now, if you wanted to buy a big position, where would you go?
You'd go to where the sellers are, because you can't buy anything unless somebody is selling it to you.

And now they've got what they came for, so price goes up.
That's it.
That's the whole thing.
The dip wasn't the move… the dip was somebody getting filled.

So the turn is when that stops.
LIVE
3 down close candles… there, there, there.

1 candle just undid three…
The thing that was happening has stopped happening.
I call this my 3 candle rotation...
That's delivery being shifted.
Now I want a second opinion, from a bigger timeframe…
A 1 minute chart can show you whats not there
LIVE
Any 3 hourly candles in a row.
The middle one is the one that dips down and takes the liquidity.
Then the third closes back above the middle.
That's a swing low... The hour agrees.
So if the 9am candle takes the level and the 10am closes back inside… what should the 11am do?
It should go up… And that's exactly what it does.
That's the 3 candle swing structure... It's confirmation for your direction.
It is not where you buy…
It's what tells you buying is worth doing.
If you treat your hourly candles as your daily candles, a whole new world opens up.

1- Your stop goes below the low that just got swept.
